newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGER LASHES REFEREE, OPPONENTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGER LASHES REFEREE, OPPONENTS.

text.p: British Lions manager Fran Cotton hit out at the referee and Northern Free State players after the bruising 67-39 win on Tuesday.

"It was a totally unsatisfactory game all round," he said. "No touring team should be made to play on this kind of rock hard pitch and the indiscipline of both the Northern Free State players and the referee was totally unacceptable.
"There is a combie (minibus) load of injured players going back to the hotel. The players aren't complaining, but it is the management's responsibility to see that they are looked after.
"There were several incidents of stamping on heads and we will be viewing the video of the game tonight and taking appropriate action. We have 24 hours to cite."
Prop Jason Leonard (thigh), scrumhalf Kyran Bracken (shoulder), hooker Mark Regan (shin) and wing Tony Underwood (thigh) were all injured.
But England flanker Neil Back, who scored one of the Lions' 10 tries, said: "It was a hard physical game but I didn't see any of the alleged kicks in the head or stamping".
South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) representative Alex Broun would not comment about the alleged foul play but defended the home province on the issue of the pitch.
"SARFU stands totally behind the Northern Free State Rugby Union. This ground is used for Currie Cup matches and we believe its facilities are top class," he said.
Lions' coach Ian McGeechan would not be drawn. "I'm not prepared to comment on the incidents until I've seen the video," he said.
"All I can say is that on this tour we have tried to play the game with the right spirit and attitude. We've got one game to go and that's all I'm concentrating on."
The Lions management will make a decision on any further action on Wednesday.
